findings.F1: Sense 1 definition says uncountable noun / not much / less, instead of plural noun / not many / fewer.
findings.F2: Usage note gives less and least (less people, the least mistakes) as the comparative and superlative of few.
findings.F3: Inflections omit the real comparative and superlative fewer and fewest.
findings.F4: The few versus a few contrast is restated in core idea, both explanations, usage note, and adaptation.
findings.F5: Sense 2 example 'Could I borrow a few money?' is ungrammatical (a few with uncountable money).
findings.F6: The frequent idiom few and far between is missing from phrases.
findings.F7: Quite a few (a fairly large number) is listed as a collocation of the small-number sense instead of a phrase.
findings.F8: Neutral bare few after every, the, the last, the next (every few days) is not covered by either sense.

missed: Sense 1 explanation says bare few always has a negative feel, but few after a determiner (the last few days, the next few weeks, these few) is neutral; neither the contradiction nor these uses are covered.
